item.desc: Which one do you prefer? China can look completely different during the day versus the night, and both are stunning in its own way! During our recent trip to China, we explored ancient towns and mountains during the day, and experience the vibrant city life at night. If you are thinking about a trip to China, save this guide and follow for more China travel inspo!  🌃 CHONGQING 🟢 Hongyadong 洪崖洞 is best visited around sunset so you can see it before and after the lights turn on.  🟢 Liziba Station 李子坝站 is where Chongqing’s Line 2 monorail appears to travel directly through a building.  🟢 Luohan Temple 罗汉寺 is a peaceful Buddhist temple surrounded by Chongqing’s skyscrapers. 🐼 CHENGDU 🟢 Visit the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding early in the morning when pandas tend to be more active. 🟢 Head to Chunxi Road and Taikoo Li after dark for shopping, food and the giant 3D panda screen. 🟢 Tower of Life is especially impressive after dark when the structure is illuminated. ⛰️ ZHANGJIAJIE 🟢 Allow at least 2 - 3 days for Zhangjiajie National Forest Park. Highlights include Yuanjiajie, Tianzi Mountain and the Bailong Elevator. 🟢 Stay near Wulingyuan for easier access to the national park. 🟢 Add Tianmen Mountain if you have another day. It is a separate attraction closer to Zhangjiajie city. 🏮 FURONG TOWN 🟢 This ancient town is built directly around a waterfall and is best experienced after dark when the buildings illuminate. 💧 DUJIANGYAN 🟢 Visit the Dujiangyan Irrigation System, an engineering project dating back more than 2,000 years that still helps control and distribute water today. 🟢 After dark, head into Dujiangyan city to see the famous glowing blue water known online as the Blue Tears. 🌆 GUANGZHOU 🟢 Head to the Canton Tower and the Zhujiang New Town waterfront around sunset. Stay after dark to see the tower and Guangzhou’s modern skyline illuminated along the Pearl River. 🟢 Explore Yongqing Fang 永庆坊 and the surrounding Xiguan area for historic Cantonese architecture alongside restored shops, cafés and restaurants. 🟢 Make time for Dim Sum while you’re here! Guangzhou is one of the best places to experience traditional Cantonese morning tea.

contents.desc: Which one do you prefer?

China can look completely different during the day versus the night, and both are stunning in its own way! During our recent trip to China, we explored ancient towns and mountains during the day, and experience the vibrant city life at night. If you are thinking about a trip to China, save this guide and follow for more China travel inspo!
🌃 CHONGQING
🟢 Hongyadong 洪崖洞 is best visited around sunset so you can see it before and after the lights turn on.
🟢 Liziba Station 李子坝站 is where Chongqing’s Line 2 monorail appears to travel directly through a building.
🟢 Luohan Temple 罗汉寺 is a peaceful Buddhist temple surrounded by Chongqing’s skyscrapers.
🐼 CHENGDU
🟢 Visit the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding early in the morning when pandas tend to be more active.
🟢 Head to Chunxi Road and Taikoo Li after dark for shopping, food and the giant 3D panda screen.
🟢 Tower of Life is especially impressive after dark when the structure is illuminated.
⛰️ ZHANGJIAJIE
🟢 Allow at least 2 - 3 days for Zhangjiajie National Forest Park. Highlights include Yuanjiajie, Tianzi Mountain and the Bailong Elevator.
🟢 Stay near Wulingyuan for easier access to the national park.
🟢 Add Tianmen Mountain if you have another day. It is a separate attraction closer to Zhangjiajie city.
🏮 FURONG TOWN
🟢 This ancient town is built directly around a waterfall and is best experienced after dark when the buildings illuminate.
💧 DUJIANGYAN
🟢 Visit the Dujiangyan Irrigation System, an engineering project dating back more than 2,000 years that still helps control and distribute water today.
🟢 After dark, head into Dujiangyan city to see the famous glowing blue water known online as the Blue Tears.
🌆 GUANGZHOU
🟢 Head to the Canton Tower and the Zhujiang New Town waterfront around sunset. Stay after dark to see the tower and Guangzhou’s modern skyline illuminated along the Pearl River.
🟢 Explore Yongqing Fang 永庆坊 and the surrounding Xiguan area for historic Cantonese architecture alongside restored shops, cafés and restaurants.
🟢 Make time for Dim Sum while you’re here! Guangzhou is one of the best places to experience traditional Cantonese morning tea.

item.desc: China never fails to amaze me. 🇨🇳✨ Every time I think I’ve seen it all, it surprises me with something completely unexpected. This time, I discovered a place that feels like it came straight out of a sci-fi movie—a retro cyberpunk-style food hall hidden in the heart of Changsha. Imagine neon lights glowing from every corner, vintage storefronts blending seamlessly with futuristic design, creating a space that feels like stepping into a cyberpunk dream. ⚡🍜💫 But the most unbelievable part? A real cable car slowly glides right through the food hall. 🚡🤯 Yes, an actual cable car passes overhead while people are enjoying their meals, making it feel as if you’re dining in another dimension where the past and the future exist together. What surprised me even more is that hardly anyone seems to talk about this place online. It’s such an underrated hidden gem, full of creativity, atmosphere, and incredible attention to detail. Every corner has its own story, and every glowing light feels carefully designed to transport you somewhere else. And the food? Absolutely incredible. I tried the crayfish 🦞—rich, spicy, packed with flavor, and honestly the best I’ve ever had. I couldn’t stop eating! 🔥 If you’re ever visiting Changsha, don’t miss this place. It’s much more than a restaurant—it’s an unforgettable journey through time, imagination, and some of the best food you’ll find in the city. 🌃💖 📍Wenheyou (文和友) 36 Xiangjiang Middle Road, Tianxin District, Changsha, China #chinatravel #visitchina #chinathroughmyeyes #rimmasjourney #changsha

item.desc: American traveler shocked by fast food in China  One thing you may not know is that in China they also have international brands that you would see in the United States. They have our clothing stores they have our fast food, and it’s shocking the differences. Here when you go to fast food, usually the quality is pretty good and the price is so cheap. McDonald’s for example, has so many items that are one dollar or less than a dollar. And KFC here serves burgers and coffee while Pizza Hut is more of a sitdown, fine dining restaurant. #fyp #tellme #traveltiktok #china #usa

item.desc: Winter in China can look like this: warm sea, bare feet on the beach, and kids spending most of the day outside. Hainan works especially well for family trips because you don’t need to fill every hour with sightseeing. A good day can simply be breakfast, beach time, a slow afternoon at the resort, then seafood or local Hainan dishes in the evening. It’s also an easy contrast if the rest of your China trip is packed with cities, trains and sightseeing. For families traveling in winter, a few days in Hainan can make the whole trip feel much more balanced. Go China Now can help plan the hotel, transport and family-friendly route. DM “HAINAN” for our 5-day guide and itinerary. #beachholiday #sanya #hainan #chinatravels #falimytravel #seaview

Between the carved spiral staircases, glowing bookshelves, floating bubbles and fantasy-like ceiling, it feels like the kind of place where you’d wait for an owl to swoop down with your Hogwarts acceptance letter. The library is scheduled to officially open in August 2026—so save this hidden gem for your future China trip. Would you actually come here to read, or spend the entire time staring at the ceiling? #ChinaTravel #HiddenChina #Wuyuan #TiankengLibrary #harrypotterfans
